item.title: LEGO Shares First Glimpse of Brand-New Astro Bot Set
item.description:
PlayStation's Astro Bot is officially returning in LEGO form, as the company has unveiled a new set based on the 2024 Game of the Year winner. The LEGO Astro Bot set is due for release on October 1 for LEGO Insiders and October 4 for everyone else. This set is available exclusively as a free gift with purchase of the LEGO PlayStation set releasing the same day.

Astro Bot has quickly become PlayStation's new mascot character after the success of games like the VR title Astro Bot Rescue Mission and the 3D platformer Astro Bot . The lovable little robot was even featured in the PlayStation 5's pack-in game Astro's Playroom , which served to showcase the features of the PS5 and DualSense controller. Now, Astro Bot is accompanying the PlayStation once again with its first foray into the LEGO realm.

LEGO Fan Transforms Toy Story Lotso Set Into Pokemon's Slowpoke With No Extra Pieces

One talented LEGO builder has turned the official Toy Story Lotso set into the Gen 1 Pokemon Slowpoke without using any additional pieces.

1
By Drew Swanson

LEGO Astro Bot Set Officially Revealed

  • Pieces: 276
  • Set # 40899
  • Ages 18+
  • Price: Free Gift with Purchase
  • Release Date: October 1 for LEGO Insiders, October 4 for everyone else

Although the LEGO Astro Bot set was leaked back in July of this year, no images of the set were shared. Now that the set has officially been confirmed, fans are getting their first look at how PlayStation's latest mascot has been rendered in LEGO. Astro Bot will be fully posable in this LEGO set, and builders will be able to completely rotate the robot's head and arms, as well as swap out eyes for different expressions. The set also comes with a stand and plaque that includes the Astro Bot logo.

The LEGO figure stands over 8 inches high, 4.5 inches wide, and 2.5 inches deep, with the stand included. However, a core part of Astro Bot's character, which is the different PlayStation-themed outfits players can unlock in Astro Bot , is not represented in this LEGO set. Still, the accuracy and posability of this LEGO Astro Bot set make for an impressive build on its own, and even more so considering it's a free gift with purchase.

To get this LEGO Astro Bot , fans will have to pick up the new LEGO PlayStation set, which retails for $179. This might be a somewhat hefty price, but it isn't too bad given LEGO's track record of premium price tags and the fact that it includes a bonus Astro Bot freebie. The LEGO PlayStation set depicts the original PS1 console and even includes hidden Easter eggs for iconic PlayStation franchises like Ape Escape and Gran Turismo , which were a key part of this OG console's success.

Without a firm release window for the PS6, the future of PlayStation is still up in the air. However, the popularity of Astro Bot means it's likely that the little robot will play a major role in the company's plans for its next flagship console.

item.title: Pokemon Fans Are Split Over New Pokemon Emerald Release
item.description:
A new Pokemon release featuring Emerald 's Hoenn Region has fans divided over whether it's necessary. The Gen 3 Pokemon games remain some of the most beloved entries in the franchise, and many fans point to them as the pinnacle of what the series is capable of. However, not all fans consider Pokemon Emerald perfect, with one fan going out of their way to create a new version of the Hoenn Region that more accurately reflects its real-life counterpart.

It's hardly fair to say that Pokemon Emerald is a controversial game, especially when it introduced the fan-favorite Battle Frontier to the post-game along with the ability to rematch trainers and Gym Leaders. With Pokemon Ruby, Sapphire, and Emerald leaked for Nintendo Switch, it's likely Gen 3 oldheads will get to experience the Hoenn Region all over again very soon. In the meantime, players looking for a take on Hoenn that's accurate to its real-life inspiration, a dedicated Pokemon fan has created the Pokemon Emerald Rotate ROM hack for fans to experience.

You Can Now Play Pokemon on YouTube

A pair of talented YouTubers have created a way to play Pokemon directly on the platform, allowing players to catch, battle, explore, and more.

By Drew Swanson

Pokemon Emerald Rotate Spins the Hoenn Region's Map by 90 Degrees

Pokemon Emerald Rotate comes from modder HexManiacAdvance and features a new take on the Hoenn Region's map that is, as the name implies, rotated by 90 degrees to the right. The justification for this change, according to the ROM hack's creator, is that the original orientation of Hoenn's map differs from the real-world Japanese region of Kyushu that it's based on by a rotation of 90 degrees. To solve this issue, HexManiacAdvance simply rotated every part of Hoenn's map by 90 degrees so that north is no longer to the left of the screen, but up, as they feel it should have been originally.

The existence of this ROM hack has Pokemon fans divided over whether it actually improves Pokemon Emerald . Twitter users responding to the announcement of Pokemon Emerald Rotate shared a mixture of confusion at the new perspective of the game's map and enthusiasm for the creator's commitment to solving a problem they didn't know they had. So many Pokemon fans have already played through Emerald enough times to have the Hoenn Region memorized, so this release is sure to mess with many players' heads.

As some Twitter users note, an infamous location like the Sky Pillar, which requires players to precisely navigate breakable tiles, will be much harder in this Pokemon ROM hack. Aside from rotating the map to accurately match Kyushu, Pokemon Emerald Rotate also adds certain Pokemon that aren't available in the base game as rare spawns. Otherwise, everything else is true to the original, vanilla version of Pokemon Emerald .

An official, non-rotated version of Pokemon Emerald and the other Hoenn games could be hitting the Nintendo Switch soon. A recent post from the official Japanese Pokemon Twitter account showcased what appears to be the first look at Ruby and Sapphire running on the Switch. No release date for these games has officially been confirmed, but signs point towards Pokemon Ruby, Sapphire, and Emerald hitting the Switch in the very near future.
